context: A uni student interviews a retired builder at home
purpose: Teach: 土木/兵隊/戦線/母子/次男/長女/膜/芯

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 戦後の土木業界に長く携わってこられたんですよね。
lines.en: You spent a long time working in postwar civil engineering, didn't you?
lines.style: Respectful, genuinely curious. Soft opener — not presuming. Lean-in quality, like settling in to listen carefully.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、私は次男坊でね、長女の姉が家計を支えてくれていた。
lines.en: Yes. I was the second son — my older sister carried the weight of the family finances.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact recollection, tinged with gratitude. Measured pace. The slight distance of memory — not dwelling, just stating what was.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: お父様は兵隊として戦線に出られたんでしょうか。
lines.en: Did your father go to the front as a soldier during the war?
lines.style: Careful, considerate phrasing. Soft enough not to presume the answer. Gives space for him to say yes or no without shame either way.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん。戻ってきてから、母子だけの家を建て直すのに必死だった。
lines.en: Yes. After he came home, he was consumed with rebuilding — supporting just my mother and himself.
lines.style: Quiet, steady voice carrying the weight underneath. No embellishment. The gravity lives in the simplicity of what he's saying.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 当時の現場、鉛筆の芯一本でも貴重だったと聞きました。
lines.en: I've heard that on worksites back then, even a single pencil lead was precious.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost musing. Not probing — offering what he knows and inviting confirmation. Respectful of the knowledge he's drawing out.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうだ。紙も薄い膜のようで、すぐ破れた。
lines.en: Exactly. Paper was thin as membrane — it would tear at the slightest touch.
lines.style: Voice shifts into vividness. He can see it. A small pause before the physical detail — like the image is clear in his mind. Sharp, specific.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 貴重なお話、ありがとうございます。
lines.en: Thank you for sharing these stories with me.
lines.style: Genuine gratitude, quietly sincere. Not effusive. The respect in his voice is understated but solid — he means it.
